---
title: "Raspberry Pi Application"
---

## Role of the Raspberry Pi

The Raspberry Pi implements the high-level control layer of the prototype. It is responsible for:

- displaying the operator interface through the GFX HAT;
- reading PNG files from the USB flash drive;
- copying the selected pattern to local storage;
- validating the PNG dimensions and number of colours;
- mapping RGB colours to the commands `C1`, `C2` and `C3`;
- communicating with the ESP32 through USB serial;
- displaying the current processing progress;
- hosting the error-recognition pipeline.

## Integrated Script

The active user-interface and machine-control program is:

```text
raspberry.py
```

### Main Software Classes

| Class | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `GfxScreen` | LCD drawing, progress bar, touch LEDs and RGB backlight |
| `PatternApp` | Interface states, touch events, file discovery and screen rendering |
| `UsbMachineController` | PNG validation, serial port, ESP32 messages and progress |
| `DemoController` | Interface simulation without real ESP32 actuation |

## Pattern Processing

The Raspberry Pi checks that the selected image:

- is a valid image readable as RGB;
- has width equal to 48 pixels;
- contains exactly three distinct colours.

The image pixels are read sequentially. The first distinct colour is mapped to `C1`, the second to `C2`, and the third to `C3`.

## USB Serial Communication

The Raspberry Pi connects to the ESP32 using:

```text
/dev/ttyUSB0
115200 baud
```

The serial-reading loop is executed in a worker thread. In this way, waiting for the physical microswitch does not freeze the display interface or the capacitive buttons.

## Raspberry Pi Commands

### Virtual Environment

```bash
source /home/aless/venvs/uncinetto/bin/activate
```

### Detect the ESP32 Port

```bash
python3 -m serial.tools.list_ports -v
```

### Mount the Pattern USB Drive

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/pattern_usb
sudo mount /dev/sda1 /mnt/pattern_usb
ls -lah /mnt/pattern_usb
```

### Start the Integrated Application

```bash
python3 /home/aless/raspberry.py --usb-dir /mnt/pattern_usb --port /dev/ttyUSB0
```

## Vision Integration

The error-recognition algorithm is executed on the Raspberry Pi and is designed to inspect the yarn configuration near the hook. The interface already provides the event:

```python
app.notify_error()
```

The final closed-loop step is to connect this recognition event to the physical machine pause/stop behavior.
